items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: So the only one I didn’t know that well was J.R. because he was already gone playing when I started.

ctx.x: That’s right. Come between Rochester — you know I have, I don’t know if this is part of the question but I’m going to say it here — I have an affinity here for Upstate New York because I’m from Pittsburgh and I’ve been living in New York for about 35 years. But I grew up in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. And I went to school at Youngstown State University. And why that’s relevant is there was a guy that was going to school at the time, he just got off of Woody Herman’s band, his name was Tony Leonardi. And he was from…

It wasn’t part of the curriculum really except for it was an elective. So my point is that Tony turned me on to all kinds of great, you know he heard I played — I auditioned for the band. I didn’t know the band. I just auditioned for the band, I made it, and we started becoming with friends, and he turned me on to all these hip — then I remember he invited Sal Nistico to the school, so we could hear him, you know? And he played with us, and then I got to know Sal. Now again when I moved to New York I moved to…
And all these Upstate guys are, you know their last name always ends with a vowel.
